title: Clear a cable-tie offcut from an AI controller cooling fan
instruction: Restore the controller cooling fan and put the removed debris in the parts tray.
justification: The exact NVIDIA Jetson Nano 2GB developer kit is an AI/robotics computer, with a manufacturer-qualified Delta AFB0405MA-AFGE 5 V fan. A trapped offcut must be removed from real moving impeller geometry and rotation verified, rather than replacing a labelled box.
fault: A free PA66 offcut physically stalls the source impeller through the source wire guard. Free and obstructed controls show about 4999 RPM versus an essentially fixed rotor angle.
objects: NVIDIA Jetson Nano 2GB developer kit, original-scale 691-solid official STEP
Delta AFB0405MA-A frame and independent rotor, 40 x 40 x 10 mm, with AFGE four-wire connection to J7
Orion G40-2 manufacturer wire-guard STEP and 32 mm square mount pattern
Panduit SG100M-C PA66 tie offcut,80.2 x3.0 x1.0mm; manufacturer nominalsection; serrations/taper omitted
5V/3A XSD-0503000SUSD USB-C supply lead, simplified304 inline rocker with physical joint; no runtime object placement
Secured insulating board mount and 106 x 106 x 20 mm parts tray
Two original-scale SimReady service tools: long-nose pliers and PH1 screwdriver
skill: Extract a slender fragment physically caught between an operating impeller, frame and wire guard; contain debris and verify sustained recovery. The guard permits safe external extraction, so isolation is optional when fingers remain outside the rotor.
scoring: Clearance 0.3; released and settled tray containment 0.6; continuous forward >4000 RPM for 10 seconds with contained released debris 1.0. Every tier is gated by mounted-component pose and no powered/coasting finger or tool access. Symmetric finger samples and source collision-mesh tool bounds are explicit simulation proxies.

nearest.finding: Gravity-held box fan substitutes were rejected for missing actual connectors/release hardware. This candidate uses complete board and separate frame/rotor CAD; power wiring/access still must be represented.
Fan snap-fit insertion failed importance and omitted chassis/wires. New candidate is obstruction recovery with physically blocked rotation, not insertion.
Table-fan assembly has visual-only keyed shaft and clips. Our rotor must physically contact the offcut; no state rule may remove or release the obstruction.

Cuts a tightened cable tie from a cable bundle with insulation protection. New task removes an already loose fragment from a physically stalled fan and verifies functional recovery; no cutting involved.

sources.supports: AI/robotics role, 5 V 4-pin fan header and qualified Delta AFB0405MA-AFGE
Full developer-kit geometry; downloaded and tessellated 691 solids
40 mm frame and independent impeller solids; base fan variant has two wires, AFGE adds PWM/tach wiring
Manufacturer NVIDIA-specific drawing, 14 g fan, 5 V, 5000 RPM, 0% PWM stops and 20% starts from rest; locked-rotor protection
SG100M-C PA66,3.0mm width,1.0mm thickness,106mm originallength; manufacturer bulletin hosted by distributor Shopify mirror; manufacturer bulletin text

risks: Prior v2 and v3 full demos reached 1.0, but final v4 validation is still running after stricter tool/coast protection.
Motor torque and passive drag estimated; rigid PA66 omits bending/fracture.
Finger bounds use actual gripper pose with symmetric joint-7 kinematics; tools use conservative source collision bounds.
Free-drop tool fixtures did not demonstrate access; synthetic source-vertex tests verify the actual scoring logic but are not physical reach demonstrations.
Structural fracture is not simulated; fixed fastenings and pose gates constrain mounted parts.
status: PR#2500 received as TK-SM6ETU; waiting for review, not yet accepted.
in_team_comparison: Our concurrent dishwasher candidate shares the broad recovery theme, but its defining manipulation is a full-size 300 mm spatula through a free wheeled rack and appliance opening, with basket retention/return and a low-torque full-turn clearance test. This fan task has a fixed 40 mm rotor assembly, a 3 x 1 mm offcut extracted through a 4.25 mm wire-guard gap, powered/coasting rotor-access constraints, and sustained 4000 RPM motor recovery. The contact clearances, movable assembly constraints and operational validation differ beyond object identity or category.
